description: IBEX-derived heliopause from Reisenfeld et al. (2021), the complete original Figure 8 Z–H model/display envelope. Category 3 tail distances are ENA sounding limits, not a measured physical heliopause closure.

sourceReference.observations: IBEX-Hi ENA observations 2009–2019, correlated with earlier 1 AU solar-wind dynamic pressure; three assumed termination-shock models.
sourceReference.variant: Figure 8 cyan surface, trace 0; Zirnstein–Heerikhuisen termination-shock model
sourceReference.frame: Modified right-handed J2000 ecliptic: +X at longitude 165 degrees; +Y at 255 degrees; +Z north ecliptic pole.

categoryMeaning.1: Well-constrained upwind estimates, approximate uncertainty ±10 AU.
categoryMeaning.2: Flanks/poles and high-latitude estimates, approximate uncertainty ±15 AU.
categoryMeaning.3: Tail ENA formation-region edge, approximate ±30 AU sounding uncertainty; actual heliopause may be much farther. Not a measured tail closure.
categoryMeaning.4: Five noisy regions manually constrained by neighboring pixels or higher-energy time structure; retained as published.

sourceReference.tailDisplay: The complete envelope follows the original published figure. The ten category 3 samples (13 grid entries with seam copies) represent the detectable tail ENA region, not proof of a closed physical heliopause. All source values and categories remain available in macropixels.json.

approximation.geometry: All 91 coordinates of the complete published 13 by 7 grid remain exact in the scientific source, including repeated poles/seam and category 3 tail values. Offline radial-linear display subdivision uses four segments per original triangle edge. Radius interpolates linearly while direction is normalized; original samples remain fixed and shared edges are welded. This rounds display facets without adding scientific measurements or asserting greater source resolution. Category 3 values retain their sounding-limit classification; the closed display envelope does not locate the physical end of the tail.
approximation.normal: Area-weighted outward surface normals are prepared on the refined display mesh, including welded source seams and poles. They occupy the retained radialNormals compatibility field for material transport; they are renderer-derived surface normals, not measurements or a Sun-radial science assumption.
approximation.material: 22 nonuniform facing levels in [-1,1]; 2024 sorted corner triples. Every 32px tile evaluates the original rim equation on barycentrically interpolated corner facing values, baking linear-to-sRGB color and alpha. Six prepared corner permutations address the shared sorted bank. Quantization, raster sampling, coarse silhouettes and the interpolation of vertex-facing scalars approximate the original per-pixel shader, particularly near the boundary.
approximation.coverage: All three triangle edges use exact pixel-area coverage inside a 1.5px transparent atlas inset. Prepared expanded parallelograms map the inset triangle corners to the unchanged physical source vertices. Fractional alpha is 1-(1-opacity)^coverage, so neighboring optical depths combine correctly under ordinary source-over. No runtime clipping, mask, filter or mesh construction.
approximation.display: Current colorLinear [0.5,0.9,0.8], opacity 0.2, rimFadeFacing 0.1, visibility and unitScale 50 preserved. These are presentation choices, not the paper’s photometry or plasma brightness.
approximation.runtime: Fixed prepared triangle leaves and atlas. Scientific archives, workbook decoding, frame construction and grid triangulation remain offline.

displaySubdivision.scope: Display interpolation only; original geometry and uncertainty classification remain checked separately.

approximation.bounds: Conservative Cartesian cube with half-extent equal to the largest original source radius, 383 AU. Positive barycentric radius interpolation cannot exceed that source radius; this encloses the curved display interpolation as well as original samples.
